h: חַג הַפֶּסַח, מַאֲמָר כ״א Pesach — Maamar Kaf Aleph

p: בַּפְּסִיקְתָּא
In the Pesikta
(מִצְוַת עֹמֶר)
(Mitzvas Omer)
וּבְוַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה
and in Vayikra Rabbah
(כ"ח, ג' וּבְקֹהֶלֶת רַבָּה א', ד' בְּשִׁינּוּי קְצָת)
(28:3, and in Koheles Rabbah 1:4 with slight variation)
הֵבִיא מִקּוֹדֶם פָּסוּק מִגֶּשֶׁם
it first cites a verse concerning rain
(יִרְמְיָה ה', כ"ד):
(Yirmiyahu 5:24):
וְלֹא אָמְרוּ נִירָא אֶת ה' אֱלֹהֵינוּ הַנֹּתֵן גֶּשֶׁם יוֹרֶה וּמַלְקוֹשׁ בְּעִתּוֹ שְׁבֻעוֹת חֻקּוֹת קָצִיר יִשְׁמָר לָנוּ וְכוּלֵּי
"Neither do they say: 'Let us fear Hashem our God, Who gives rain, both the former and the latter in its season, Who reserves for us the appointed weeks of the harvest,' etc."
יִשְׁמוֹר לָנוּ מִן הַשָּׁרָב וּמִן הָרוּחוֹת קָשִׁים וּמִן הַטְּלָלִים קָשִׁים,
"Who reserves for us [protection] from scorching heat, from harsh winds, and from harmful dews,"
וְאֵלּוּ הֵן שֶׁבַע שַׁבָּתוֹת תְּמִימוֹת שֶׁבֵּין פֶּסַח לַעֲצֶרֶת.
and these are the seven complete weeks between Pesach and Shavuos.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ אִיתָא:
And afterward it is stated:
אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: סַנְטִירָךְ אֲנָא וְלֵית אַתְּ יָהֵיב לִי סַנְטֵרוּתִי!
"Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: [Israel say to God,] 'I am Your vineyard-watchman (santeir), and You do not give me my watchman's wage?!'"
אָמַר רַבִּי בְּרֶכְיָה: מַגְרִיסָךְ אֲנָא וְלֵית אַתְּ מַטְעִים לִי מִן תַּבְשִׁילָךְ דְּנֵדַע מָה אִינוּן צְרִיכִין, אִם טַל אִם מָטָר!
"Rabbi Berechyah said: 'I am Your grain-grinder/cook, and You do not let me taste from Your dish so that we may know what they need, whether dew or rain!'"
הוּא שֶׁדָּוִד אָמַר
This is what David said
(תְּהִלִּים ס"ח, י'):
(Tehillim 68:10):
גֶּשֶׁם נְדָבוֹת תָּנִיף וְגוֹמֵר
"A generous rain You wave (tanif), etc."
אִם גֶּשֶׁם הִיא צְרִיכָה, נְדָבוֹת; אִם טַל הִיא צְרִיכָה, תָּנִיף אֱלֹהִים
"if it needs rain, [send] generous [rains]; if it needs dew, wave it, O God"
עַיֵּין שָׁם בְּמַתְּנוֹת כְּהוּנָּה וּבְפֵירוּשׁ הַגְּרָ"א לַפְּסִיקְתָּא.
(see there in Matnos Kehunah and in the Vilna Gaon's commentary on the Pesikta).
אַךְ יֵשׁ לְהָבִין:
However, one must understand:
דְּאִם נְפָרֵשׁ "סַנְטִירָךְ אֲנָא" כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר מִקּוֹדֶם "יִשְׁמוֹר לָנוּ מִן הַשָּׁרָב",
if we explain "I am Your watchman" in reference to what was said earlier, "Who reserves/guards for us from scorching heat,"
וְקָשֶׁה: דְּאִם כֵּן הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְצַוּוֹת לְהַקְרִיב עֹמֶר בְּאֶחָד דְּפֶסַח,
then it is difficult: if so, the Torah should have commanded to offer the Omer on the first day of Pesach,
וְעוֹד דְּה' יִתְבָּרַךְ נִקְרָא סַנְטֵר אַחַר כָּךְ בְּהַשֶּׁבַע שַׁבָּתוֹת וְלֹא קוֹדֶם!
and furthermore, it is Hashem, may He be blessed, Who is called the watchman afterward during the seven weeks, not beforehand!
וְאִם נְפָרֵשׁ "סַנְטִירָךְ אֲנָא" מַה שֶּׁה' יִתְבָּרַךְ שָׁמַר עַל הַפֶּתַח בְּמִצְרַיִם וְלֹא יִתֵּן הַמַּשְׁחִית לָבוֹא וְגוֹמֵר,
And if we explain "I am Your watchman" as referring to Hashem, may He be blessed, guarding the doorway in Egypt and not allowing the Destroyer to enter, etc.,
מַה זֶּה טַעַם עַל מִצְוַת הָעֹמֶר שֶׁנּוֹהֵג בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל?!
how is that a reason for the mitzvah of the Omer, which applies only in the Land of Israel?!
גַּם מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ "מַגְרִיסָךְ אֲנָא וְכוּלֵּי וְלֵית אַתְּ מַטְעִים לִי מִן תַּבְשִׁילָךְ דְּנֵדַע מָה אִינוּן צְרִיכִין אִם טַל אוֹ מָטָר",
Also, regarding what they said, "I am Your cook, etc., and You do not let me taste from Your dish so that we may know what they need, whether dew or rain"
קָשֶׁה: הָא זְמַן הַגְּשָׁמִים כְּבָר עָבַר!
it is difficult: surely the rainy season has already passed [by Pesach]!
וְאַחַר כָּךְ אִיתָא
And afterward it is stated
(ibid.):
אָמַר רַבִּי בְּנָאָה: כְּשֶׁהָיִיתִי נוֹתֵן לָכֶם אֶת הָעֹמֶר, הָיִיתִי נוֹתֵן לְכָל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד עֹמֶר לַגֻּלְגֹּלֶת וְכוּלֵּי, לְפִיכָךְ מֹשֶׁה מַזְהִיר אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל: וַהֲבֵאתֶם עֹמֶר
"Rabbi Bena'ah said: [God says,] 'When I gave you the Omer [of manna], I gave each and every one an omer per head, etc.; therefore Moshe warns Israel: And you shall bring an omer'"
וְיֵשׁ לְהָבִין אֵיךְ אָמַר טַעַם לְמִצְוַת הָעֹמֶר שֶׁנּוֹהֵג בְּכָל דּוֹר מֵהַמָּן שֶׁהָיָה רַק בַּמִּדְבָּר, וּבַמִּדְבָּר לֹא הִקְרִיבוּ הָעֹמֶר עַד שֶׁבָּאוּ לְאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל?!

and one must understand how it gives a reason for the mitzvah of the Omer—which applies in every generation [in the Land]—from the manna which existed only in the wilderness, whereas in the wilderness they did not offer the Omer until they entered the Land of Israel?!
אַךְ עִנְיַן "סַנְטִירָךְ אֲנָא" — הַשְּׁמִירָה מִכָּל רַע מִקִּטְרוּג הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע, שֶׁאִלְמָלֵא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שֶׁעוֹזֵר לוֹ אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לוֹ

However, the meaning of "I am Your watchman" is Divine protection from all evil and from the prosecution of the evil inclination, for were it not for the Holy One, blessed is He, helping man, he could not overcome it
(סוּכָּה נ"ב:);
(Sukkah 52b);
וּ"מַגְרִיסָךְ אֲנָא" — שֶׁה' יִתְבָּרַךְ הַמַּאֲכִיל, וְעִיקַּר קִטְרוּג יֵצֶר הָרָע מִתּוֹךְ אֲכִילָה וּשְׁתִיָּה
and "I am Your feeder/cook" means that Hashem, may He be blessed, is the One Who feeds us, for the primary prosecution of the evil inclination arises out of eating and drinking
(סִפְרֵי עֵקֶב ז' וּשְׁאָר מְקוֹמוֹת),
(Sifrei Eikev 7 and other places),
שֶׁתְּחִילַּת הַסָּתַת הַנָּחָשׁ הָיָה בְּתַאֲוַת אֲכִילָה;
since the serpent's initial incitement was through the lust for eating;
וּכְשֶׁמַּכִּיר שֶׁה' יִתְבָּרַךְ מַאֲכִיל, אָז אֵין דָּבָר רַע בָּא מִזֶּה וְאֵין יֵצֶר הָרָע מֵאֲכִילָה זוֹ.
and when one recognizes that Hashem, may He be blessed, is the One providing the food, then no evil comes from it and the evil inclination has no hold through this eating.
וּבַמִּדְבָּר הָיָה ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ הַמַּאֲכִיל מָן, וְהָיָה אֲכִילָה בִּקְדוּשָּׁה שֶׁיִּתְיַשֵּׁב דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה בְּגוּפָן
And in the wilderness, Hashem, may He be blessed, was the One feeding them manna, which was eating in holiness so that words of Torah would settle into their bodies
(תַּנְחוּמָא בְּשַׁלַּח א'),
(Tanchuma Beshalach 1),
וְכֵן כָּל אֲכִילָה בִּקְדוּשָּׁה נִקְרָא "מָן", כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא
and likewise all eating in holiness is called "manna," as they said in the Gemara
(סוּכָּה ל"ט:)
(Sukkah 39b)
עַל שָׁלֹשׁ סְעוּדּוֹת שַׁבָּת: בִּכְדֵי מָן שָׁנוּ.
regarding the three Shabbos meals: "They taught it according to the measure of manna."
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ
And this is what is said regarding our father Yaakov
(בְּרֵאשִׁית כ"ח, כ'):
(Bereishis 28:20):
וּשְׁמָרַנִי בַּדֶּרֶךְ הַזֶּה
"And He will guard me on this path"
שֶׁלֹּא אֶלְמַד מִמַּעֲשֵׂה לָבָן, וְזֶהוּ "סַנְטִירָךְ אֲנָא";
that I should not learn from Lavan's deeds, and this is "I am Your watchman";
וְנָתַן לִי לֶחֶם לֶאֱכֹל וְגוֹמֵר
"and He will give me bread to eat, etc."
הַיְינוּ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ הַמַּאֲכִיל, וְזֶהוּ "מַגְרִיסָךְ אֲנָא".
meaning that Hashem, may He be blessed, be the One feeding me, and this is "I am Your feeder."

p: וְהִנֵּה בַּפְּסִיקְתָּא אַחַר כָּךְ אִיתָא:
Now in the Pesikta afterward it is stated:
לֹא תְּהֵא מִצְוַת עֹמֶר קַלָּה בְּעֵינֵיכֶם, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי מִצְוַת עֹמֶר זָכָה אַבְרָהָם וְיָרַשׁ אֶת אֶרֶץ כְּנַעַן, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
"Let not the mitzvah of the Omer be light in your eyes, for through the mitzvah of the Omer Avraham merited and inherited the land of Canaan, as it is said
(Bereishis 17:8):
וְנָתַתִּי לְךָ וּלְזַרְעֲךָ וְגוֹמֵר
'And I will give to you and to your seed, etc.'
עַל מְנָת: וְאַתָּה אֶת בְּרִיתִי תִשְׁמֹר; וְאֵיזֶה זֶה? מִצְוַת הָעוֹמֶר,
on condition of 'And you shall keep My covenant'; and what is that? The mitzvah of the Omer."
וְתָמְהוּ עַל זֶה: מַה שַּׁיָּיכוּת עֹמֶר לִבְרִית?
And commentators wondered at this: what connection does the Omer have to the covenant of circumcision (bris)?
וְהַגְּרָ"א זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה פֵּירֵשׁ מִגְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה דְּ"תָּמִים", וּבָעֹמֶר כְּתִיב "תְּמִימֹת",
And the Vilna Gaon, of blessed memory, explained it through a gezeirah shavah of the word tamim ("wholesome/complete"), since regarding the Omer it is written temimos ("complete weeks"),
וְתָמַהּ עַל זֶה דְּהָא "תְּמִימֹת" בִּסְפִירַת הָעֹמֶר כְּתִיב, וְהִנִּיחַ בְּצָרִיךְ עִיּוּן.
yet he himself wondered at this because temimos is written regarding the counting of the Omer [not the Omer offering], and left it requiring further study.
אַךְ אִיתָא מֵהָאֲרִיזַ"ל דִּימֵי הַסְּפִירָה מְסוּגָּלִים לְתִיקּוּן פְּגַם הַבְּרִית, וְכָתְבוּ בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר רֶמֶז לָזֶה: עֹמֶר בְּגִימַטְרִיָּא קֶרִי.

However, it is taught by the Arizal that the days of Sefiras HaOmer are uniquely propitious for rectifying the blemish of the covenant, and elsewhere an allusion to this is noted: Omer (עמר = 310) has the same numerical value as keri (קרי = 310, nocturnal emission).
וְהִנֵּה כְּבָר דִּקְדַּקְנוּ שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה נִקְרָא "חַג הַמַּצּוֹת" וּבִלְשׁוֹן חֲזַ"ל "חַג הַפֶּסַח", וְלָמָּה שִׁינּוּ מִלְּשׁוֹן הַתּוֹרָה?

Now we have already noted that in the Torah it is called "the Festival of Matzos," whereas in the parlance of the Sages it is called "the Festival of Pesach"—why did they diverge from the Torah's terminology?
וּלְבַד זֶה הַפֶּסַח נִקְרָב בְּי"ד וְנֶאֱכָל רַק לַיְלָה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה, וְלָמָּה קָרְאוּ לְכָל הֶחָג פֶּסַח?
Besides that, the Pesach sacrifice is offered on the fourteenth and eaten only on the first night—why, then, did they call the entire seven-day festival "Pesach"?
גַּם הַפֶּסַח אֵינוֹ קָרֵב רַק בִּזְמַן שֶׁבֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ קַיָּים, וְלָמָּה נִקְרָא חַג הַפֶּסַח אַחַר הַחוּרְבָּן?
Furthermore, the Pesach sacrifice is offered only when the Holy Temple stands—why is it still called the Festival of Pesach after the destruction?
וְיוֹתֵר יִתָּכֵן לִקְרוֹתוֹ חַג הַמַּצּוֹת דְּנוֹהֵג אַף בִּזְמַן הַזֶּה!
It would be far more fitting to call it the Festival of Matzos, which applies even nowadays!
גַּם כָּל שֵׁם פֶּסַח עַל שֵׁם שֶׁפָּסַח הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עַל בָּתֵּי בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּמִצְרַיִם, וְיִתָּכֵן שֶׁנִּקְרָא הַקָּרְבָּן עַל שֵׁם זֶה, אֲבָל לָמָּה יִקְרְאוּ לְכָל הֶחָג כֵּן?

Also, the entire name "Pesach" is because the Holy One, blessed is He, passed over the houses of the Children of Israel in Egypt; it makes sense that the sacrifice be named after this, but why call the entire festival so?
אַךְ מָצִינוּ בַּהַפְטָרָה:
Now we find in the Haftarah [of the second day of Pesach]:
וַיְצַו הַמֶּלֶךְ וְגוֹמֵר עֲשׂוּ פֶסַח לַה' אֱלֹהֵיכֶם כַּכָּתוּב בְּסֵפֶר הַבְּרִית הַזֶּה
"And the king [Yoshiyahu] commanded, etc.: 'Make a Pesach to Hashem your God, as is written in this Book of the Covenant'"
(מְלָכִים ב' כ"ג, כ"א)
(II Melachim 23:21)
וְאֵין לוֹ פֵּירוּשׁ: וְכִי דָּבָר חָדָשׁ מָצְאוּ?
which seems inexplicable: did they discover something new?
וַהֲוָה לֵיהּ לוֹמַר "כַּאֲשֶׁר צִוָּה ה'"!
It should have said "as Hashem commanded"!
גַּם מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר אַחַר כָּךְ:
Also, what is stated afterward:
כִּי לֹא נַעֲשָׂה כַּפֶּסַח הַזֶּה מִימֵי הַשֹּׁפְטִים וְגוֹמֵר וְכֹל מַלְכֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וּמַלְכֵי יְהוּדָה
"For there was not made such a Pesach from the days of the Judges, etc., nor in all the days of the kings of Israel and the kings of Judah"
יֵשׁ לְהָבִין אֵיךְ יִתָּכֵן שֶׁבִּימֵי דָּוִד וּשְׁלֹמֹה וּמַלְכֵי יְהוּדָה הַצַּדִּיקִים לֹא נַעֲשָׂה פֶּסַח חַס וְשָׁלוֹם,
one must understand how it is possible that in the days of David, Shlomo, and the righteous kings of Judah, Pesach was not observed, God forbid,
וּמַה זֶּה שֶׁצִּיֵּין "כַּפֶּסַח הַזֶּה"?
and what is meant by specifying "such a Pesach"?
אַךְ כְּבָר אָמַרְנוּ דְּחַג הַפֶּסַח נִקְרָא יוֹם ה' הַגָּדוֹל וְהַנּוֹרָא, מִדַּת אַבְרָהָם וְיַעֲקֹב:
However, we have already explained that the festival of Pesach is called "the great and awesome day of Hashem," embodying the attributes of Avraham and Yaakov:
שֶׁגּוּף הֶחָג, יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם, הָיָה בִּזְכוּת אַבְרָהָם וּמִדָּתוֹ חֶסֶד לְאַבְרָהָם, וְזֶהוּ "הַגָּדוֹל";
for the core of the festival, the Exodus from Egypt, was in the merit of Avraham and his attribute "Kindness to Avraham," which is "the Great";
וְהוּא גַּם כֵּן קְדוּשַּׁת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ: שְׂפַת אֱמֶת תִּכּוֹן לָעַד, שֶׁיּוּקְבַּע הָאַהֲבָה לְעוֹלְמֵי עַד,
and it is also the holiness of our father Yaakov, "a truthful lip shall be established forever," that love be permanently fixed forevermore,
וְזֶהוּ "וְהַנּוֹרָא", שְׁלֵימוּ דְּכוּלָּא
and this is "and the Awesome," the perfection of all
(זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב' ע"ח:),
(Zohar, Vol. 2, 78b),
שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה בָּהֶן דּוֹפִי כְּלָל, שֶׁנִּתְקַן כָּל שׁוֹרֶשׁ פְּגַם הַנָּחָשׁ וּפָסְקָה זוֹהֲמָא מֵאֲבוֹתֵינוּ אַחַר שְׁלֹשָׁה דּוֹרוֹת
that there be no blemish in them whatsoever, having rectified the entire root of the Serpent's blemish so that filth ceased from our forefathers after three generations
(שַׁבָּת קמ"ו.).
(Shabbos 146a).
וְתֵיכֶף בְּלַיְלָה רִאשׁוֹנָה כְּתִיב
And immediately on the first night it is written
(שְׁמוֹת י"ב, כ"ג):
(Shemos 12:23):
וּפָסַח ה' עַל הַפֶּתַח וְלֹא יִתֵּן הַמַּשְׁחִית לָבֹא אֶל בָּתֵּיכֶם וְגוֹמֵר
"And Hashem will pass over the doorway and will not allow the Destroyer to enter your houses, etc."
הַמַּשְׁחִית הוּא הַשָּׂטָן, הוּא הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע, הוּא מַלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת
the Destroyer is Satan, is the evil inclination, is the Angel of Death
(בָּבָא בַּתְרָא ט"ז.),
(Bava Basra 16a),
וּמִצַּד ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ זָכוּ לְשָׁעָה לַעֲקוֹר יֵצֶר הָרָע מִלִּבָּם.
and from the side of Hashem, may He be blessed, they merited temporarily to have the evil inclination uprooted from their hearts.
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
And this is what is said
(שְׁמוֹת י"ב, י"ח):
(Shemos 12:18):
בָּעֶרֶב תֹּאכְלוּ מַצֹּת,
"In the evening you shall eat matzos,"
שֶׁמּוֹרֶה שֶׁאֵין עוֹד שְׂאוֹר בְּעִיסָּה כְּלָל, רַק בְּשָׁנָה רִאשׁוֹנָה אֵין חִימּוּצוֹ נוֹהֵג אֶלָּא יוֹם אֶחָד
which signifies that there is no longer any leaven in the dough at all, except that in the first year its chametz prohibition applied only for one day
(פְּסָחִים צ"ו:).
(Pesachim 96b).
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם הוֹפִיעַ אַחַר כָּךְ עַל יְדֵי מִצְוַת הַפֶּסַח לְכָל הַשִּׁבְעָה יָמִים:
Nevertheless, afterward it shone forth through the mitzvah of the Pesach offering across all seven days:
שִׁבְעַת יָמִים תֹּאכַל עָלָיו מַצּוֹת
"Seven days you shall eat matzos upon it"
"עָלָיו" דַּיְיקָא, שֶׁמִּצְוַת הַפֶּסַח הוֹפִיעַ בְּכָל הַשִּׁבְעָה יָמִים,
specifically "upon it," because the mitzvah of the Pesach offering radiated throughout all seven days,
וְעִיקַּר הַמִּצְוָה שֶׁיֵּעָקֵר הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע מִכֹּל וָכֹל כְּמוֹ אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן קוֹדֶם הַקִּלְקוּל, קְדוּשַּׁת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
and the essence of the mitzvah is that the evil inclination be completely uprooted just like Adam HaRishon before the sin, the holiness of our father Yaakov, peace be upon him,
שֶׁעַל שֵׁם זֶה נִקְרָא הֶחָג יוֹם ה' הַנּוֹרָא.
on account of which the festival is called "the awesome day of Hashem."
אַךְ זֶה לֹא זָכוּ עֲדַיִין לְעוֹלָם, כִּי לָזֶה צָרִיךְ הִתְגַּלּוּת עַתִּיקָא;
However, they had not yet merited this permanently, because for that a revelation of Atika is required;
וּבְלַיְלָה רִאשׁוֹנָה זָכוּ מִצַּד ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְאַחַר כָּךְ בִּקְרִיעַת יַם סוּף "רָאֲתָה שִׁפְחָה וְכוּלֵּי" הָיָה הָרְאִיָּה,
so on the first night they merited it from Hashem's side, and afterward at the Splitting of the Sea—"A maidservant saw, etc."—there was prophetic vision,
וּבְמַתַּן תּוֹרָה שֶׁזָּכוּ לָזֶה, דִּכְתִיב
and at the Giving of the Torah they merited it, as it is written
(תְּהִלִּים פ"ב, ו'):
(Tehillim 82:6):
אֲנִי אָמַרְתִּי אֱלֹהִים אַתֶּם,
"I said, you are angelic beings,"
דְּלָא הֲווֹ מַיְיתֵי
so that they would not die
(עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ה'.),
(Avodah Zarah 5a),
אַךְ נִתְקַלְקֵל וְנִשְׁבְּרוּ הַלּוּחוֹת.
yet they sinned and the Tablets were shattered.
וְהִנֵּה בְּיֹאשִׁיָּהוּ מָצִינוּ שֶׁהָיָה סָבוּר שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ חֶרֶב שֶׁל שָׁלוֹם לֹא תַּעֲבוֹר בְּאַרְצְכֶם
Now regarding King Yoshiyahu, we find that he thought that not even a sword of peace would pass through their land
(תַּעֲנִית כ"ב:),
(Taanis 22b),
וְזֶה יִהְיֶה רַק לֶעָתִיד.
which will only occur in the Messianic future.
אַךְ בֶּאֱמֶת כְּתִיב לְמַעְלָה
Indeed, it is written earlier
(מְלָכִים ב' כ"ג, ג'):
(II Melachim 23:3):
וַיַּעֲמֹד הַמֶּלֶךְ וְגוֹמֵר וַיִּכְרֹת אֶת הַבְּרִית לִפְנֵי ה' לָלֶכֶת אַחַר ה' וְלִשְׁמֹר מִצְוֹתָיו וְגוֹמֵר בְּכָל לֵב וּבְכָל נֶפֶשׁ לְהָקִים אֶת דִּבְרֵי הַבְּרִית וְגוֹמֵר
"And the king stood, etc., and made a covenant before Hashem, to walk after Hashem and to keep His commandments, etc., with all heart and with all soul, to uphold the words of this covenant, etc."
"בְּכָל לֵב וּבְכָל נֶפֶשׁ" מוֹרֶה כְּשֶׁזּוֹכִין לְשַׁבָּת עִילָּאָה, תְּשׁוּבָה עִילָּאָה, בִּינָה, וְאִתְפְּנֵי יֵצֶר הָרָע מִתַּמָּן מִכֹּל וָכֹל לְעוֹלָם
"with all heart and with all soul" signifies when one merits the Supernal Shabbos, Supernal Repentance, Binah, from which the evil inclination is completely and permanently cleared out
(תִּיקּוּנֵי זֹהַר תִּיקּוּן מ"ח).
(Tikkunei Zohar, Tikkun 48).
וּבֶאֱמֶת הוֹעִיל הוּא בְּכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל לְשַׁעְתּוֹ,
And in truth he succeeded in effecting this throughout all Israel for that moment,
כֵּיוָן שֶׁהוּא עָשָׂה תְּשׁוּבָה שְׁלֵימָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁהֵעִיד הַכָּתוּב
because he performed complete repentance, as Scripture testifies
(מְלָכִים ב' כ"ג, כ"ה):
(II Melachim 23:25):
וְכָמֹהוּ לֹא הָיָה לְפָנָיו מֶלֶךְ אֲשֶׁר שָׁב אֶל ה' וְגוֹמֵר,
"And like him there was no king before him who returned to Hashem, etc.,"
וּגְדוֹלָה תְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁמַּגַּעַת עַד כִּסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד
and great is repentance, for it reaches up to the Throne of Glory
(יוֹמָא פ"ו.),
(Yoma 86a),
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: עַד ה'
as it is said, "unto Hashem"
וְהַיְינוּ כָּל שֵׁם הֲוָיָ"ה שֶׁהוּא תֵּשַׁע מִדּוֹת
which is the entire Name Havayah comprising nine attributes
(זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג' רנ"ח.)
(Zohar, Vol. 3, 258a)
וְתָגוֹ שֶׁל יוּ"ד דִּלְעֵילָּא, כֶּתֶר עֶלְיוֹן
and the upper tip of the Yud above, Kesser Elyon
(ibid. 14b),
וְזֶהוּ עַד כִּסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד, עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר
and this is "up to the Throne of Glory," along the lines of what is said
(Daniel 7:9):
עַד דִּי כָרְסָוָן רְמִיו וְעַתִּיק יוֹמִין יְתִב.
"Until thrones were placed and the Ancient of Days sat."
וְאִיתָא בְּסֵפֶר יְצִירָה
And it is stated in Sefer Yetzirah
(Chapter 6):
לֵב בַּנֶּפֶשׁ כְּמֶלֶךְ בַּמְּדִינָה
"The heart in the soul is like a king in a country"
(עַיֵּין זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג' קכ"ו:),
(see Zohar, Vol. 3, 126b),
וְהַמֶּלֶךְ לֵב הָעָם, וּפָעַל לְשַׁעְתּוֹ בְּלֵב כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל לְהוֹפִיעַ לָהֶם תְּשׁוּבָה עִילָּאָה, בִּינָה, שֶׁהוּא רַק בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת עַתִּיקָא,
and the king is the heart of the nation, so he effected for that moment in the hearts of all Israel to shine upon them Supernal Repentance, Binah, which comes only through a revelation of Atika,
וּמִשּׁוּם הָכִי הָיָה סָבוּר שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ חֶרֶב שֶׁל שָׁלוֹם לֹא תַּעֲבוֹר,
and therefore he thought that not even a sword of peace would pass through,
רַק שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁאֵין דּוֹרוֹ דּוֹמֶה יָפֶה
except he did not know that his generation was not genuinely upright
(תַּעֲנִית שָׁם),
(Taanis, ibid.),
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁלֹּא הוֹעִיל רַק לְשָׁעָה,
meaning it was effective only temporarily;
וְאָז הָיָה הוּא מָשִׁיחַ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
and at that moment he was Mashiach, as it is said
(אֵיכָה ד', כ'):
(Eichah 4:20):
רוּחַ אַפֵּינוּ מְשִׁיחַ ה' וְגוֹמֵר אֲשֶׁר אָמַרְנוּ בְּצִלּוֹ נִחְיֶה בַגּוֹיִם.
"The breath of our nostrils, the anointed of Hashem, etc., of whom we said, 'In his shadow we shall live among the nations.'"
רַק אָז אַחַר הַבְּרִית הַזֶּה כְּתִיב:
Immediately after this covenant it is written:
וַיְצַו הַמֶּלֶךְ וְגוֹמֵר עֲשׂוּ פֶסַח לַה' אֱלֹהֵיכֶם כַּכָּתוּב בְּסֵפֶר הַבְּרִית הַזֶּה
"And the king commanded, etc.: 'Make a Pesach to Hashem your God, as is written in this Book of the Covenant'"

וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁיֵּעָקֵר יֵצֶר הָרָע מִכֹּל וָכֹל וְיוֹפִיעַ הַקְּדוּשָּׁה בְּכָל הַשִּׁבְעָה יָמִים, שֶׁמּוֹרֶה לְעוֹלָם: שִׁבְעַת יָמִים תֹּאכַל עָלָיו מַצּוֹת, שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה שְׂאוֹר שֶׁבְּעִיסָּה כְּלָל כִּקְדוּשַּׁת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ.

meaning that the evil inclination would be totally uprooted and holiness would shine across all seven days, signifying eternity—"seven days you shall eat matzos upon it"—with no leaven in the dough whatsoever, like the holiness of our father Yaakov.
וְאָמַר הַכָּתוּב טַעַם עַל זֶה שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת כֵּן הָיָה:
And Scripture gives the reason that indeed it was so:
כִּי לֹא נַעֲשָׂה כַּפֶּסַח הַזֶּה דַּיְיקָא מִימֵי הַשֹּׁפְטִים וְגוֹמֵר
"For there was not made such a Pesach"—specifically such a Pesach—"from the days of the Judges, etc."
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁפֶּסַח כָּזֶה הָיָה רַק בְּשָׁנָה רִאשׁוֹנָה שֶׁהָיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל מְשׁוּקָּעִים בְּאַרְבָּעִים וְתֵשַׁע שַׁעֲרֵי טוּמְאָה בִּקְלִיפַּת מִצְרַיִם כְּעוּבָּר בְּבֶטֶן אִמּוֹ,
meaning that such a Pesach occurred only in the first year when Israel were sunk in the forty-nine gates of impurity within the husk of Egypt like a fetus in its mother's womb,
וְאַחַר שֶׁהֶחֱזִירָן בִּתְשׁוּבָה זָכוּ בְּ"עֶרֶב תֹּאכְלוּ מַצּוֹת" שֶׁהָיָה תְּשׁוּבָתָם עַד כִּסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד;
and after he brought them back in repentance they merited "in the evening you shall eat matzos," for their repentance reached up to the Throne of Glory;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בִּימֵי דָּוִד וּשְׁלֹמֹה שֶׁהָיוּ בֶּאֱמֶת צַדִּיקִים, לֹא זָכוּ לְפֶסַח כָּזֶה בִּשְׁלֵימוּת כַּכָּתוּב בְּסֵפֶר הַבְּרִית,
whereas in the days of David and Shlomo, who were truly righteous, they did not merit such a Pesach in full perfection as written in the Book of the Covenant,
רַק בִּימֵי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ שֶׁהִכְנִיסָן לְאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל, אָז נַעֲשָׂה גַּם כֵּן כַּפֶּסַח הַזֶּה, שֶׁלֹּא חָשַׁב הַכָּתוּב רַק מִימֵי הַשֹּׁפְטִים שֶׁאַחַר יְהוֹשֻׁעַ.
only in the days of Yehoshua when he brought them into the Land of Israel was such a Pesach also made, which is why Scripture counts only "from the days of the Judges" who came after Yehoshua.
וְהַטַּעַם: שֶׁאָז הוּקְרַב רִאשׁוֹנָה אֶת הָעֹמֶר, שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן בְּרִית.
And the reason is that then the Omer was offered for the very first time, which is also a covenant (bris).
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ: לֹא תְּהֵא מִצְוַת עֹמֶר קַלָּה בְּעֵינֶיךָ, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי מִצְוַת עֹמֶר זָכָה אַבְרָהָם וְיָרַשׁ אֶת הָאָרֶץ
And this is what they said: "Let not the mitzvah of the Omer be light in your eyes, for through the mitzvah of the Omer Avraham merited and inherited the land"
וְהַיְינוּ כִּירוּשָּׁה שֶׁאֵין לָהּ הֶפְסֵק
meaning like an inheritance that has no interruption
(בָּבָא בַּתְרָא קכ"ט:)
(Bava Basra 129b)
וְזֶה זָכָה רַק עַל מְנָת: וְאַתָּה אֶת בְּרִיתִי תִשְׁמֹר; וְאֵיזֶה זֶה? מִצְוַת עֹמֶר.
and this he merited solely on condition of "And you shall keep My covenant; and what is that? The mitzvah of the Omer."
וְהַיְינוּ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ: סַנְטִירָךְ אֲנָא
And this is what they meant by "I am Your watchman"
וְהַיְינוּ הַשּׁוֹמֵר מִכָּל רַע, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וְלֹא יִתֵּן הַמַּשְׁחִית לָבוֹא וְגוֹמֵר,
meaning He Who guards from all evil, as it is said, "And He will not allow the Destroyer to enter, etc.,"
וְהַיְינוּ בְּלֵיל רִאשׁוֹן דְּפֶסַח: וּפָסַח ה' עַל הַפֶּתַח וְגוֹמֵר;
which was on the first night of Pesach, "And Hashem passed over the doorway, etc.";
וְלֵית אַתְּ יָהֵיב לִי סַנְטֵרוּתִי
"and You do not give me my watchman's wage?!"
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁאַחַר יוֹם רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁהָיָה חִימּוּצוֹ נוֹהֵג אַף בְּשָׁנָה רִאשׁוֹנָה, אָז מַתְחִיל הַזְּמַן מִצַּד יִשְׂרָאֵל לִהְיוֹת מְזוּקָּק שִׁבְעָתַיִם,
meaning that after the first day—during which its chametz prohibition applied even in the first year—then begins the time from Israel's side to be refined sevenfold,
וְאָז מִצְוַת הָעֹמֶר כִּבְיָכוֹל שְׂכַר שְׁמִירַת ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ בַּלַּיְלָה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה,
and then the mitzvah of the Omer is, as it were, the reward/counterpart for the protection of Hashem, may He be blessed, on the first night,
וְאָז הַזְּמַן לְתַקֵּן מִדַּת צַדִּיק יְסוֹד עוֹלָם.
for then is the opportune time to rectify the attribute of Tzaddik, Foundation of the World (Yesod).
וְכֵן אִיתָא
And so it is stated
(עוּקְצִין ג', י"ב):
(Uktzin 3:12):
עָתִיד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְהַנְחִיל לְכָל צַדִּיק וְצַדִּיק ש"י עוֹלָמוֹת, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
"In the future the Holy One, blessed is He, will bequeath to each and every righteous person 310 (shai) worlds, as it is said
(מִשְׁלֵי ח', כ"א):
(Mishlei 8:21):
לְהַנְחִיל לְאֹהֲבַי יֵשׁ
'To bequeath substance (yeish = 310) to those who love Me'"
לְשׁוֹן "לְכָל צַדִּיק וְצַדִּיק" הַיְינוּ שׁוֹמֵר הַבְּרִית, שֶׁזֶּה נִקְרָא צַדִּיק
the phrase "to each and every righteous person" refers to one who guards the covenant, for he is called Tzaddik
(זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב' כ"ג.),
(Zohar, Vol. 2, 23a),
וְזֶה זוֹכֶה לְש"י עוֹלָמוֹת, גִּימַטְרִיָּא עֹמֶר וְגִּימַטְרִיָּא קֶרִי הַהִיפּוּךְ;
and such a person merits 310 worlds, the gematria of Omer (עמר = 310) and the gematria of its opposite, keri (קרי = 310);
וּכְתִיב "לְהַנְחִיל לְאֹהֲבַי", שֶׁזֶּה בִּזְכוּת הָאַהֲבָה, מִדַּת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ, דִּכְתִיב
and it is written "to bequeath to those who love Me," which is in the merit of love, the attribute of our father Avraham, as it is written
(יְשַׁעְיָה מ"א, ח'):
(Yeshayahu 41:8):
אַבְרָהָם אֹהֲבִי
"Avraham, My beloved"
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ שֶׁבִּזְכוּת הָעֹמֶר זָכָה אַבְרָהָם וְיָרַשׁ אֶת אֶרֶץ כְּנַעַן עַל מְנָת: וְאַתָּה אֶת בְּרִיתִי תִשְׁמֹר.
and this is what they said, that in the merit of the Omer Avraham merited and inherited the land of Canaan on condition of "And you shall keep My covenant."
וּכְתִיב: וְאֹצְרֹתֵיהֶם אֲמַלֵּא,
And the verse continues: "And their treasuries I will fill,"
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר
along the lines of what is said
(Yeshayahu 33:6):
יִרְאַת ה' הִיא אוֹצָרוֹ,
"The fear of Hashem is his treasure,"
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁה' יִתְבָּרַךְ מְמַלֵּא אוֹצַר צַדִּיק שֶׁהוּא יִרְאַת ה', שֶׁאִלְמָלֵא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹזְרוֹ אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לוֹ.

meaning that Hashem, may He be blessed, fills the treasure of the righteous person—which is the fear of Hashem—for were it not for the Holy One, blessed is He, helping him, he could not overcome his inclination.
וְזֶה עִנְיַן מַה שֶּׁמּוּבָא
And this is the meaning of what is brought
(זֹהַר חֵלֶק א' קכ"ג: בְּתוֹסֶפְתָּא):
(Zohar, Vol. 1, 123b, in the Tosefta):
אַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת שֶׁקֶל כֶּסֶף — אַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת עוֹלָמוֹת וְכִיסּוּפִין וַהֲנָאוֹת וְכוּלֵּי,
"Four hundred shekels of silver—four hundred worlds of yearnings and delights, etc.,"
שֶׁהוּא ש"י עוֹלָמוֹת, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: לְהַנְחִיל לְאֹהֲבַי יֵשׁ, וְצַדִּיק עוֹלָמוֹת מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: וְאֹצְרֹתֵיהֶם אֲמַלֵּא
which correspond to the 310 worlds of "to bequeath substance to those who love Me," and the worlds of the Tzaddik of "and their treasuries I will fill"
(וְנִתְבָּאֵר בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר).
(as explained elsewhere).

That is, the primary purpose of the mitzvah of the Omer is that eating matzah should be effective in eradicating the leaven in the dough—which is the corruption of the Serpent that injected lust and bodily gratification into eating—and through the mitzvah of the Omer this effect endures forever, as stated, which is "And you shall keep My covenant."
וְכָל דּוֹר הַמִּדְבָּר שֶׁאָכְלוּ רַק מָן לֹא הוּצְרְכוּ לָעֹמֶר כְּלָל, שֶׁה' יִתְבָּרַךְ הָיָה הַמַּאֲכִילָם תָּמִיד;
And the entire wilderness generation, who ate exclusively manna, had no need for the Omer at all, because Hashem, may He be blessed, was constantly feeding them directly;
רַק בְּבוֹאָם לָאָרֶץ הוּצְרְכוּ לָעֹמֶר שֶׁיּוּקְבַּע אֲכִילַת מַצָּה מִפֶּסַח לְעוֹלָם לְבַעֵר הַשְּׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָּה לְעוֹלָם.
only upon entering the Land did they require the Omer so that the holiness of eating matzah from Pesach would become permanently fixed to eradicate the leaven in the dough forever.
וְאַף שֶׁבְּשָׁנָה שְׁנִיָּה זָכוּ: שִׁבְעַת יָמִים תֹּאכַל מַצּוֹת, אֲבָל שֶׁיִּשָּׁאֵר כָּךְ לְעוֹלָם נִצְרָךְ טַלָּא דְּעַתִּיקָא,
And although in the second year they already merited "seven days you shall eat matzos," nevertheless for it to remain so permanently required the Dew of Atika
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ: מָה אִינוּן צְרִיכִין, אִם טַל.
and this is what they meant by "what they need, whether dew."

(נְדָרִים כ"ב:),
(Nedarim 22b),

grasping everything directly from the Written Torah just as Moshe Rabbeinu merited everything from Sinai—and such a person needs "rain."

And this is what is said: "A generous rain You wave, O God"
אִם גֶּשֶׁם נְדָבוֹת, שֶׁזֶּהוּ זוֹכֶה מִנְּדָבָה שֶׁמַּגִּיעַ לוֹ מִנִּדְבַת לִבּוֹ;
if "a generous rain," that is for one who merits it through generosity, coming to him from the generosity of his own heart;
אִם טַל תָּנִיף אֱלֹהִים וְגוֹמֵר, שֶׁזֶּה מִצַּד ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיַּעֲזוֹר לְבַעֵר כָּל הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע וְהַשְּׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָּה לְעוֹלָם.
if "dew, You wave, O God, etc.," that is from the side of Hashem, may He be blessed, Who helps to eradicate all the evil inclination and the leaven in the dough forever.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Sod Yesharim, First Day of Pesach 14 — “Knesses Yisrael asked improperly, ‘Let Him come to us like rain,’ which is sometimes requested and sometimes not, and the Holy One, blessed is He, answered her properly, ‘I will be like dew to Israel,’ a thing always requested. Rain denotes the Will clothed within human grasp; dew, what is still in will and desire without any garment… But Knesses Yisrael could ask from their side only for rain, that the good be explicit within their grasp through the toil of their service; yet Hashem answered, ‘I will be like dew,’ the source of the Will from which all salvations are drawn.” Connection: The same pairing of rain with what is reached by human effort and dew with what comes from God’s side alone, as in this maamar’s reading of “if dew, You wave it.”

Now from the side of Hashem, may He be blessed, it is "Pesach," that Hashem passed over the houses of the Children of Israel and did not allow the Destroyer to enter, so as to eradicate the evil inclination;
וּמִצַּד יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל יְדֵי אֲכִילַת מַצָּה זוֹכִין עַל יְדֵי הָעֹמֶר שֶׁיּוּקְבַּע קְדוּשַּׁת אֲכִילַת מַצָּה בְּלֵב יִשְׂרָאֵל לְבַעֵר הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע לְעוֹלָם.
and from the side of Israel, through eating matzah, they merit by means of the Omer that the holiness of eating matzah becomes fixed in the heart of Israel to eradicate the evil inclination forever.
וְזֶה הַטַּעַם שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב, שֶׁהוּא קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא תּוֹרָה אִיקְרֵי
And this is the reason why in the Written Torah—since "the Holy One, blessed is He, is called Torah"
(זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב' ס'.)
(Zohar, Vol. 2, 60a)
נִקְרָא הֶחָג "חַג הַמַּצּוֹת", שֶׁה' יִתְבָּרַךְ תּוֹלֶה הַקְּדוּשָּׁה בִּפְעוּלַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּקִיּוּם מִצְוַת אֲכִילַת מַצָּה;
the festival is called "the Festival of Matzos," because Hashem, may He be blessed, attributes the holiness to Israel's action in fulfilling the mitzvah of eating matzah;
וּבְתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, וְכֵן אֲנַחְנוּ קוֹרִין הֶחָג עַל שֵׁם הַפֶּסַח: אֲשֶׁר פָּסַח ה' וְגוֹמֵר,
whereas in the Oral Torah—and likewise we ourselves—call the festival after "Pesach," "Who passed over, etc.,"
שֶׁאַף אֲכִילַת מַצָּה שֶׁלָּנוּ הוּא רַק עַל יְדֵי עֵזֶר ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ אֲשֶׁר פָּסַח וְגוֹמֵר וְלֹא יִתֵּן הַמַּשְׁחִית וְגוֹמֵר,
recognizing that even our eating of matzah is only through the help of Hashem, may He be blessed, "Who passed over, etc., and will not allow the Destroyer, etc.,"
שֶׁלֹּא יָבוֹא הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע הַמַּחְמִיצֵנוּ לְהַטּוֹת לְבָבֵנוּ לְמַשְׁחִית חַס וְשָׁלוֹם.
so that the evil inclination that sours us should not come to turn our hearts toward destruction, God forbid.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּפְּסִיקְתָּא לְמַעְלָה:
And this is what they said in the Pesikta cited above:
שְׁבֻעוֹת חֻקּוֹת [קָצִיר] יִשְׁמָר לָנוּ — יִשְׁמוֹר לָנוּ מִן הַשָּׁרָב וּמִן הָרוּחוֹת קָשִׁים וּמִן הַטְּלָלִים קָשִׁים.
"'Who reserves for us the appointed weeks of the harvest'—He will guard us from scorching heat, from harsh winds, and from harmful dews."
שָׁרָב הַיְינוּ קְלִיפַּת הַקִּנְאָה שֶׁהִיא אֵשׁ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
"Scorching heat" (sharav) refers to the husk of envy, which is fire, as it is said
(אֶסְתֵּר א', י"ב):
(Esther 1:12):
וַחֲמָתוֹ בָּעֲרָה בוֹ,
"And his wrath burned within him,"
וְכֵן קְלִיפַּת הַתַּאֲוָה נִקְרָא אֵשׁ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
and similarly the husk of lust is called fire, as it is said
(Hoshea 7:4):
כֻּלָּם מְנָאֲפִים כְּמוֹ תַנּוּר בֹּעֵרָה מֵאֹפֶה,

וּבַגְּמָרָא
and in the Gemara

(Kiddushin 81a):
כִּי עַמּוּדָא דְּנוּרָא חָזֵי, דְּאַתְּ נוּרָא וְכוּלֵּי;

and "from harsh winds" (ruchos) refers to evil desires/wills;

and "harmful dews" refers to evil thoughts
(וְנִתְבָּאֵר בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר).
(as explained elsewhere).
אֵימָתַי? שֶׁבַע שַׁבָּתוֹת תְּמִימוֹת שֶׁבֵּין פֶּסַח לַעֲצֶרֶת
When does this protection apply? During the "seven complete weeks between Pesach and Shavuos"
דִּקְדֵּק "תְּמִימוֹת", דְּהַיְינוּ שֶׁמּוֹעִיל רַק כְּשֶׁהֵן תְּמִימוֹת כְּסִדְרָן, שֶׁמְּבָרֵר אֶת עַצְמוֹ בְּכָל הַמִּדּוֹת שֶׁבַע פְּעָמִים שֶׁבַע לִהְיוֹת מְזוּקָּק שִׁבְעָתַיִם,

אָז מוֹעִיל "לְהַנְחִיל לְאֹהֲבַי יֵשׁ וְאֹצְרֹתֵיהֶם אֲמַלֵּא",
then it is effective "to bequeath substance to those who love Me, and their treasuries I will fill,"
לְהִשָּׁמֵר מִשָּׁרָב, מִקְּלִיפַּת הָאֵשׁ שֶׁכּוֹלֵל כָּל שָׁלֹשׁ הַקְּלִיפּוֹת: קִנְאָה תַּאֲוָה וְכָבוֹד

(which are three times eish [fire = 301], as explained elsewhere regarding the 903 [3 × 301] forms of death)

(according to the reading of Vayikra Rabbah),
אוֹ לְגִירְסָא: שֶׁהַשְּׁכִינָה בֵּינֵיהֶם, שֶׁהֵבִיא הַגְּרָ"א זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה
or according to the reading "when the Divine Presence is among them," cited by the Vilna Gaon, of blessed memory
וּמִקּוֹדֶם פֵּירֵשׁ כִּפְשׁוּטוֹ: תְּמִימוֹת מִצַּד יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁסּוֹפְרִין כְּסִדְרָן לְהִתְבָּרֵר לִהְיוֹת מְזוּקָּק שֶׁבַע פְּעָמִים שֶׁבַע,
whereas first it explained it in its plain sense: "complete" from Israel's side, that they count in proper order to be refined and purified seven times seven,
אָז יִשְׁמוֹר לָנוּ מִן הַשָּׁרָב וְכוּלֵּי, וְיִזְכּוּ אַחַר כָּךְ לַטַּל, אִם צְרִיכִים, אוֹ מִי שֶׁזּוֹכֶה לַגֶּשֶׁם,
and then He will guard us from the scorching heat, etc., and they will merit afterward the "dew," if they need it, or whoever merits the "rain,"
וְאַחַר כָּךְ בְּשָׁבוּעוֹת הַזְּמַן לִזְכּוֹת לְמַתַּן תּוֹרָה כְּמוֹ בְּלוּחוֹת רִאשׁוֹנוֹת וְכָאָמוּר.
and afterward on Shavuos is the opportune time to merit the Giving of the Torah just as at the First Tablets, as stated.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Pesach 4 — “The Mishnah’s distinction between the Pesach of Egypt, whose chametz was forbidden one day, and the Pesach of the generations, all seven, is because we know in ourselves that all our power to eat matzah and remove the leaven is only what flows from Hashem, the power of the passing-over. And so in the language of the Sages it is called the Festival of Pesach, and we call the festival by the name of the Holy One, blessed is He, for all is from His side; and in the language of the Torah it is called the Festival of Matzos, for Hashem calls it by our deeds, as though everything were done from our side.” Connection: The same account of the festival’s two names, joined to the same Mishnah on chametz for one day in Egypt and seven in later generations.
